match.reason: No point in the bank covers the political approach to management, where groups compete for power and managers negotiate and build alliances, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: The political approach
card: The political approach sees a business as a collection of groups, such as departments, teams and owners. Each group has its own interests and goals.
These groups compete for limited power and resources, such as budget, staff and equipment. Their interests can clash.
Managers work by negotiating with groups and building alliances, where groups agree to back each other's goals.
Decisions are shaped by bargaining and influence. They are not simply set by rules or by the manager alone.
draft.remember: Groups compete for power and resources, so managers negotiate and build alliances.

a.q: Which situation best shows the political approach in a business?
opts: Two teams argue over budget and a manager brokers a deal
A manager writes a strict rulebook for every worker
A manager times each task and pays by items made
A manager reshapes the business as the market changes
a.why: The political approach is about groups with different interests competing for resources, and a manager negotiating between them. A rulebook relies on set rules and authority, not bargaining.
a.clue: Look for groups with different interests and a deal between them.

b.q: At Harbour Toys in Newcastle, the design team wants more money for new products. The warehouse team wants new shelving. Both want the same limited budget. The manager meets each team and agrees to back design this year in return for warehouse support next year. What is the manager doing?
opts: Negotiating and building an alliance between groups
Breaking the work into simple, measured tasks
Ending the competition by giving orders from the top
Paying each team by how much it produces
b.why: The manager is bargaining with groups that compete for a limited budget, and trading support for later support. That is negotiating and building an alliance. Giving orders from the top would not use bargaining, so it does not fit this case.
b.clue: The manager trades support with each group instead of ordering them.

problems.detail: "agrees to back design this year in return for warehouse support next year" is ambiguous. It could mean the warehouse team supports design (or the manager) next year, rather than the warehouse getting its turn at the budget next year. Rewording, e.g. "in return for backing the warehouse next year", would make the trade clear.
